boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented SMU rituals and recurring celebrations, from Dallas Hall ceremonies to Mustang game-day customs.

cards.title: Walk the Rotunda Passage
cards.subtitle: Opening Convocation and May Baccalaureate • Dallas Hall
cards.notes: Notice the two directions of the ritual: new students enter through Dallas Hall, while graduating students make their final campus walk out.
cards.short_summary: Dallas Hall frames both the formal welcome to SMU and the symbolic departure at graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU identifies the Rotunda Passage as a symbolic tradition comprising a processional for entering students and a recessional for graduates.
cards.access_notes: Occurs within scheduled Opening Convocation and Baccalaureate ceremonies; ceremony participation is directed by SMU.

cards.title: Pass the Howard Lantern
cards.subtitle: May Baccalaureate Service
cards.notes: Look for the lantern handoff from the senior class president to a junior-class representative during the May Baccalaureate Service.
cards.short_summary: A lantern handoff represents the continuing light of learning between SMU classes.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU states that the Howard Lantern is handed annually at May Baccalaureate from the senior class president to a junior-class representative.
cards.access_notes: Presented during SMU's scheduled May Baccalaureate Service.

cards.title: Watch the Ovilla Curtain Fall
cards.subtitle: Opening Convocation • McFarlin Auditorium
cards.notes: At the close of Opening Convocation, watch for the historic curtain to lower—the ceremonial signal that the new class's initiation is complete.
cards.short_summary: A historic McFarlin Auditorium fire curtain closes SMU's formal welcome for new students.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU says the Ovilla Curtain is lowered at the end of Opening Convocation to signify completion of new students' initiation.
cards.access_notes: Part of the scheduled Opening Convocation ceremony in McFarlin Auditorium.

cards.title: Sing “Varsity” at the Close
cards.subtitle: Convocation, Baccalaureate, and athletics
cards.notes: Learn the alma mater before a major campus ceremony or game, then join the community when “Varsity” is sung at the close.
cards.short_summary: SMU's 1916 alma mater links academic ceremonies and sporting events.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU describes “Varsity” as its official school song, sung at Opening Convocation, December Commencement, Baccalaureate, and sporting events.
cards.access_notes: Presented at scheduled university ceremonies and athletics events.

cards.title: Make the Pony Ears
cards.subtitle: SMU spirit gesture • campus events and games
cards.notes: Start with a peace sign, relax the first two fingers slightly, and use the gesture in photos, cheers, and school-song moments.
cards.short_summary: SMU's hand sign turns a relaxed two-finger gesture into pony ears.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU instructs students to form Pony Ears with a relaxed peace sign and says the symbol is used for photos, cheering, and school songs.
cards.source_title: Celebrate SMU: History, Mascot, and Traditions | SMU
cards.access_notes: A spirit gesture used at campus occasions; follow event guidance where applicable.

cards.title: Boulevard Before Kickoff
cards.subtitle: Bishop Boulevard • SMU home football games
cards.notes: Before a home game, walk Bishop Boulevard and Dallas Hall Lawn to take in the established pregame gathering known as Boulevarding.
cards.short_summary: At SMU, the pre-football-game gathering has its own verb: Boulevarding.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU describes Boulevarding as its home-football-game tradition, with the community gathering along Bishop Boulevard and Dallas Hall Lawn.
cards.source_title: Experience Campus Life at SMU | SMU
cards.access_notes: Takes place before scheduled SMU home football games; follow current game-day and venue guidance.

cards.title: See the Pigskin Revue
cards.subtitle: Homecoming Weekend
cards.notes: Check the Homecoming program for the variety show, where student groups, faculty, alumni, and the Mustang Band take the stage.
cards.short_summary: A Homecoming variety show has brought SMU community acts together since 1933.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU calls Pigskin Revue its longest-running tradition and says the Homecoming variety show began in 1933.
cards.source_title: Celebrate SMU: History, Mascot, and Traditions | SMU
cards.access_notes: Presented during scheduled Homecoming Weekend programming; consult the current event program.

cards.title: Celebrate PerunaPalooza
cards.subtitle: Spring • Peruna's birthday celebration
cards.notes: Find the spring birthday festival for SMU's live mascot, then spend time with its games, rides, and campus activities.
cards.short_summary: SMU marks its mascot Peruna's birthday with a spring festival.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU states that PerunaPalooza is held every spring to celebrate Peruna's birthday and includes games, rides, and activities.
cards.source_title: Celebrate SMU: History, Mascot, and Traditions | SMU
cards.access_notes: A spring event; confirm the current date, location, and entry details with SMU programming.

cards.title: Wait for Dallas Hall to Light Up
cards.subtitle: Holiday season • Dallas Hall Lawn
cards.notes: Gather on the Dallas Hall lawn for student carols, then stay through “Silent Night” for the lighting of the building.
cards.short_summary: Dallas Hall's holiday illumination is the finale of SMU's seasonal community gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU says Celebration of Lights gathers the community for carols and concludes with the lighting of Dallas Hall after “Silent Night.”
cards.source_title: Celebrate SMU: History, Mascot, and Traditions | SMU
cards.access_notes: A holiday-season event; verify the current program details before attending.

cards.title: Spot the “Diamond M”
cards.subtitle: SMU football game performances
cards.notes: At a football game, watch the Mustang Band's field presentation for its documented “Diamond M” formation and feature twirler.
cards.short_summary: The Mustang Band's signature field formation turns the SMU initial into a diamond-shaped M.
cards.evidence_claim: SMU identifies the Mustang Band's “Diamond M” formation as part of its spirit-and-traditions presentation.
cards.access_notes: Seen during scheduled football-game band performances; stadium entry and viewing follow current event rules.
